### Home

File: `src/app/features/home/home.ts`
Selector: `app-home`
Standalone: yes
Change detection: `ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush`

Description: Protected landing page: shows who the token says you are. It also calls the backend's /api/hello through the dev proxy, which is what turns this from "the browser can read a token" into proof that the backend accepted it too — the Phase 1 definition of done.

Properties:
- `auth: unknown = inject(AuthService)`
- `backendError: unknown = signal<string | null>(null)`
- `backendIdentity: unknown = signal<HelloResponse | null>(null)`
- `http: unknown = inject(HttpClient)`
- `realmRoles: unknown = this.auth.realmRoles`
- `username: unknown = this.auth.username`

Methods:
- `signOut(): void`

### Login

File: `src/app/features/login/login.ts`
Selector: `app-login`
Standalone: yes
Change detection: `ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush`

Description: Login view: the trigger for the redirect to Keycloak. The redirect is started by an explicit click rather than automatically on load. An automatic redirect turns any transient Keycloak error into a redirect loop the user cannot escape.

Properties:
- `auth: unknown = inject(AuthService)`
- `router: unknown = inject(Router)`

Methods:
- `signIn(): void`

## Services / Injectables

### AuthService

File: `src/app/core/auth/auth.service.ts`
providedIn: `root`

Description: Wraps angular-oauth2-oidc so components never touch the OIDC library directly. Roles are read from the access token , not the ID token: Keycloak puts realm roles in realm\_access.roles there. They drive what the UI shows — the backend enforces the same roles server-side, because hiding a button is not a security control (NFR-3).

Properties:
- `authState: unknown = signal(0)` — Bumped after every login/logout so the derived signals recompute.
- `isAuthenticated: unknown = computed(() => { this.authState(); return this.oauth.hasValidAccessToken(); })`
- `oauth: unknown = inject(OAuthService)`
- `realmRoles: unknown = computed(() => { this.authState(); return this.claims()?.realm_access?.roles ?? []; })`
- `username: unknown = computed(() => { this.authState(); return this.claims()?.preferred_username ?? ''; })`

Methods:
- `claims(): AccessTokenClaims | null` — Decodes the access token payload; returns null when there is no valid token.
- `init(): Promise<void>` — Configures the client, fetches the discovery document and completes a redirect that is coming back from Keycloak. Runs once during application startup.
- `login(): void` — Sends the browser to Keycloak's login page.
- `logout(): void`

## Guards

### authGuard

File: `src/app/core/auth/auth.guard.ts`

Description: Blocks routes for callers without a valid access token and sends them to /login. This is convenience, not security: every protected resource is enforced again by the backend resource server, which is the only place an authorization decision actually counts (NFR-3).

## Interfaces

### AccessTokenClaims

File: `src/app/core/auth/auth.service.ts`

Description: Shape of the Keycloak access token claims this application reads.

Properties:
- `preferred_username?: string`
- `realm_access?: { roles?: string[] }`

### HelloResponse

File: `src/app/features/home/home.ts`

Description: What GET /api/hello returns — the backend's view of the caller.

Properties:
- `roles: string[]`
- `username: string`

- `authConfig: AuthConfig = { issuer: environment.keycloakIssuer, clientId: environment.keycloakClientId, responseType: 'code', redirectUri: window.location.origin + '/home', postLogoutRed…` — OIDC client configuration for the Keycloak realm maintenance (ADR-003). Authorization Code Flow with PKCE: the browser is a public client that cannot keep a secret, so PKCE replaces the client secret. responseType: 'code' plus disablePKCE: false is what makes this the code flow rather than the deprecated implicit flow.
  Defined in `src/app/core/auth/auth.config.ts`
- `environment: object = { production: false, keycloakIssuer: 'http://localhost:8081/realms/maintenance', keycloakClientId: 'frontend', apiBaseUrl: '/api', }` — Local development environment, matching the compose stack in docker/. Keycloak is reached directly on port 8081, while /api goes through the dev-server proxy (proxy.conf.json) so the browser sees a single origin and the backend needs no CORS setup.
  Defined in `src/environments/environment.development.ts`
- `environment: object = { production: true, /** Keycloak realm base URL — the OIDC issuer (ADR-003). */ keycloakIssuer: 'https://auth.example.org/realms/maintenance', /** Public client…` — Production/default environment. The values are placeholders until the Hetzner deployment exists (Phase 4); the shape is what matters, so application code never needs to know which environment it runs in.
  Defined in `src/environments/environment.ts`
